info.title: FixTag API
info.description: Incident reporting for industrial machines. Clients own machines made by one or more manufacturers, and each manufacturer's staff only see the machines it made and their incidents. Errors are returned as `{"error": "..."}` with a 4xx/5xx status.

get.summary: GET by id, returns the raw file with the Content-Type it was uploaded with

200.description: The file, with the Content-Type it was uploaded with

schema.description: Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.
Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.
Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.

post.summary:
POST, registers a client together with its first gestor. When the NIF is already registered
(the client buys from another manufacturer too) it only links the caller's organization to
it, and nothing else about the client changes. Only a manufacturer's support staff.
Online only: the NIF decides which organization the client is, so the server has to answer.

200.description: Already registered, now linked (`manager` is null)

201.description: New client, with its gestor's temporary password

400.description: Invalid NIF, empty name or invalid manager

409.description: The NIF belongs to a manufacturer, or the manager's email is in use

post.summary:
Registers the device's FCM token for push notifications. Call it after every login and
whenever Firebase rotates the token, a token moves to whoever registered it last.

get.summary:
GET with params for filtering and pagination, one endpoint serves both the lists and
the incremental sync. Ordered by last change, so every change to an incident (status,
assignment, message, attachment, edit) moves it past the cursor and it's delivered again.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor, the `next_cursor` of a previous response

parameters.name: assigned_to
parameters.description: Only the incidents assigned to this technician, e.g. a technician's own queue

put.summary:
PUT, creates the incident with the client's id, safe to retry. Sending it again later
edits the descriptive fields, which only the author can do.

404.description: Already exists, but the caller can't see it

409.description: machine_id differs from the stored incident

put.summary:
PUT, uploads one file as the request body. The id is generated by the client, re-sending
an attachment that was already stored returns it without rewriting the file.

requestBody.description: Raw file bytes, sent with the file's Content-Type (e.g. image/jpeg)

schema.description: Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.
Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.
Raw file bytes, only used to document binary bodies.

404.description: Incident not synced yet, retry after it is

409.description: attachment_id already used by another incident

413.description: File larger than the server's max_upload_bytes

415.description: Content-Type isn't image, audio or video

post.summary:
POST, appends a message, a status change and/or an assignment to the incident's history.
Returns the whole incident so the app can store the new status and assignee straight away.

200.description: Already appended (retry with the same id)

400.description: Nothing to append, or assigned_to isn't a technician of the manufacturer handling it

403.description: Status change by someone other than its support staff or assigned technician, or assignment by someone other than its support staff

409.description: Update id already used by another incident

post.summary:
When `user.must_change_password` is set the account is still on its temporary password:
every endpoint except `POST /me/password` answers 403 until it's changed.

get.summary:
Machines visible to the caller: every machine of their client, whoever made it, or the ones
their manufacturer made, at every client. Small enough to cache whole in Room, so QR lookups
also work offline.

parameters.name: serial_number
parameters.description: Exact serial number, e.g. the value read from the QR code

put.summary:
PUT, registers a machine the caller's manufacturer made, at a client it serves, with the id
generated by the app, like incidents, so it can be registered offline. Sending it again edits
the serial number and model. Only a manufacturer's support staff can.

400.description: Empty fields, or organization_id isn't a client the caller's manufacturer serves

404.description: The id belongs to another manufacturer's machine

409.description: serial_number belongs to another machine, or organization_id differs from the stored machine

post.summary:
POST, replaces the caller's password, temporary or not. Other devices are logged out (their
refresh tokens stop working), and this one gets a new pair of tokens.

400.description: Wrong current password, or the new one is too short or the same

get.summary:
The visible organizations: the caller's own, plus the manufacturers it buys from (for a
client) or the clients it serves (for a manufacturer). Small enough to cache whole, e.g. to
name a machine's owner and manufacturer, or to pick the client of a new machine.

put.summary:
PUT, renames an organization: its own gestor, or the support staff of a manufacturer that
serves it (a client).

403.description: Neither its gestor nor a manufacturer that serves it

post.summary:
Exchanges a refresh token for a new access token and a new refresh token. The old refresh
token is revoked (after a short grace period), so always store the new one.

401.description: Unknown, expired or revoked refresh token, log in again

get.summary:
The technicians of the caller's manufacturer, who its support staff can assign incidents
to, least busy first.
The people in the caller's organization, e.g. for a gestor's team screen.

post.summary:
POST, creates an account in the caller's own organization with a temporary password. There
are no emails, so the response is the only place the password appears.

400.description: Empty name, invalid email, or a role the organization doesn't have

403.description: Not allowed to create that role

Attachment.description: Metadata of an uploaded file, the content is served by `GET /attachments/{id}`.

manager.description:
The client's first gestor, who creates the rest of its accounts. Ignored when the NIF is
already registered, the client has one then

name.description: Ignored when the NIF is already registered

nif.description: The client's NIF, what tells two manufacturers they serve the same client

oneOf.description:
The new client's gestor and their temporary password, `null` when the client was
already registered and only the link to the caller's organization was added

temporary_password.description:
Shown only in this response, for whoever created the account to hand over. The new
member has to replace it at their first login

ErrorBody.description: JSON body of every error response.

assigned_to.description: Technician handling the incident, assigned by support staff

created_at.description: Server clock at the moment the incident was first received

handled_by.description: The organization whose support staff take it, the machine's manufacturer

id.description: Generated by the client, re-sending the same id never creates a duplicate

organization_id.description: The client that owns the machine

reported_at.description: Device clock at the moment the incident was created, possibly offline

updated_at.description: Bumped by any change, including new updates and attachments

updates.description: Status history and messages, oldest first

description.description: May be empty when the incident was reported by voice

latitude.description: Send latitude and longitude together, or neither

reported_at.description: Device clock when the incident was created

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` to get the next page. After the last page, keep it and pass it on the
next sync to get only the incidents that changed since. `null` only if nothing exists yet.

assigned_to.description: Technician the incident was assigned to by this entry

Technician to hand the incident to, replacing any previous one. Only support staff can
assign, and only to a `tecnico` of the manufacturer handling the incident

id.description: Optional id generated by the client, makes retries safe

oneOf.description:
Only the support staff of the manufacturer handling it (`assistencia` or `gestor`), or
the technician it's assigned to, can change the status

manufacturer_id.description: Who made it and services it, their staff see it and its incidents

serial_number.description: Also what the QR code on the machine encodes

organization_id.description:
The client that owns the machine, one the caller's manufacturer serves. Can't change
later. The manufacturer is always the caller's organization

serial_number.description: Also what the QR code on the machine encodes, unique across every client

role.description: A gestor can create any role of their organization, support staff only `tecnico`

nif.description: Portuguese tax number (NIF/NIPC), 9 digits, unique across the platform

new_password.description: At least 8 characters, different from the current one

Technician.description: Someone support staff can assign incidents to.

open_incidents.description: Incidents assigned to them that aren't resolved yet, a rough measure of how busy they are

expires_in.description: Seconds until the access token expires

refresh_token.description: Exchange at `POST /refresh` when the access token expires, single use

must_change_password.description:
Still on the temporary password they were created with. Until they change it at
`POST /me/password`, every other endpoint answers 403

organization_kind.description: Which side the user works for, the client or the manufacturer
